target: हमारे घर में हर किसी का अपना कमरा है।
english: In our house everyone has their own room.
reason: Original ('every relationship has its own importance in our home') is a vacuous textbook motto, not something anyone says. Replacement keeps the अपना possessive point with a concrete everyday fact.

target: पापा अपने दोस्तों से रोज़ फ़ोन पर बात करते हैं।
english: Papa talks to his friends on the phone every day.
reason: Original ('serves his parents with great devotion', श्रद्धा से सेवा) is preachy/moralising devotional register. Replacement teaches the same अपने + habitual present in ordinary speech.

target: ऑफ़िस के बाद मैं दोस्तों के साथ चाय पीता हूँ।
english: After office I have tea with friends.
reason: Original is confusing and stilted (देवरजी is niche kinship vocab, and 'lives with us after the wedding' leaves whose wedding unclear). Replacement keeps के बाद + के साथ in a sentence a learner would actually use.

english: Go to the market and bring some vegetables.
reason: Original is niche gardening content (क्यारी = flowerbed) a learner will never need. Replacement keeps the -कर participle + imperative with high-frequency everyday vocabulary.

target: फूल लगाकर पूरा कमरा सजाया गया।
english: The whole room was decorated with flowers.
reason: Original uses very rare literary vocabulary (चंदोवा तानकर = stretching a canopy) and reads like wedding-report prose. Replacement keeps -कर + passive with common words.

target: उस किताब में हाथ से लिखे कई नोट्स थे।
english: That book had several handwritten notes.
reason: Original (पांडुलिपि = manuscript with annotations) is bookish trivia far from everyday speech. Replacement keeps 'हाथ से लिखा' participial phrase in an ordinary context.

target: जो लड़का सामने बैठा है, वह मेरा भाई है।
english: The boy sitting in front is my brother.
reason: Original ('the bird that flies highest is the eagle') is pointless trivia and reads like a textbook line. Replacement keeps the जो…वह relative-correlative in a normal introduction.

target: जो आदमी दरवाज़े पर खड़ा है, वह हमारा पड़ोसी है।
english: The man standing at the door is our neighbour.
reason: Original ('one who helps others is liked by everyone') is a moralising proverb. Replacement keeps जो…वह with an ordinary, useful statement.

target: जब परीक्षा नज़दीक आती है, तब छात्र ख़ूब पढ़ते हैं।
english: When the exams get close, students study a lot.
reason: Original is unnatural — 'नौ दिन तक' (for nine days) is an arbitrary detail that makes no sense alongside 'during exam days'. Replacement keeps the correlative time clause naturally.

target: मौसम विभाग ने कहा है कि कल बारिश होगी।
english: The weather department said it will rain tomorrow.
reason: Original word order ('कल बारिश होगी, ऐसा मौसम विभाग ने कहा') is written translationese; spoken Hindi fronts the reporting verb with कि. Same future tense retained.
